summary:
VITAL is a wearable astronaut health-monitoring prototype combined with an interactive digital platform, developed in response to the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. It uses an ESP32-S3 microcontroller connected to a MAX30102 heart rate sensor and an MPU6050 movement sensor to collect selected health indicators. Its digital platform includes a health dashboard, educational information about the effects of space on the human body, and a daily wellbeing survey that provides recommendations based on astronauts’ responses.

VITAL addresses the challenge by bringing physical measurements and personal wellbeing information together in one accessible platform. It aims to help astronauts better understand changes in their wellbeing and recognise when they may need medical support. This is important because long-duration space missions present unique physical and psychological challenges, while immediate medical assistance may not always be available. VITAL demonstrates how wearable technology and accessible software can contribute to supporting astronaut wellbeing during future space exploration.
details:
What if astronauts could better understand their health, millions of kilometres away from Earth?

VITAL is a wearable health-monitoring prototype combined with an interactive digital platform designed for long-duration space missions.

Using an ESP32-S3, MAX30102 heart rate sensor and MPU6050 movement sensor, VITAL collects selected health indicators. Its website also features a daily wellbeing survey that provides recommendations based on astronauts’ mood, energy, sleep and physical wellbeing.

We used wearable electronics, microcontroller programming and Canva to develop our prototype and digital platform.

Our creativity lies in combining physical health measurements with personal wellbeing check-ins in one system. We considered affordability, portability, usability and the challenges of accessing medical support in space.

Our goal is simple: help astronauts better understand their wellbeing and support safer future space exploration.
